findings.reason: naming the existing consumer turns §7 from an open question into a specific producer to wire, which changes what the node builds.
findings.text: §7 asks whether reckon should verify a declared window against the endpoint it dispatches into, yet cites none of the mechanisms that already address its subject — the wired consumer `_context_fit_verdict` at `reckon/crew/routing.py:3259`, the producer-by-design `reckon/crew/context_budget.py::refusal_census` (written, unwired), and the unwired endpoint probe `reckon/crew/serving_origin.py::check_serving_origin` — so the section reads as if nothing exists where three mechanisms do

findings.reason: the node should wire `refusal_census` into the existing slot rather than build a second checker, which is a smaller change than §7's open question implies.
findings.text: §7 proposes a guard that would fire on an endpoint-vs-declared disagreement, but that guard is already written (`_context_fit_verdict`, `reckon/crew/routing.py:3238`, reading `effective_input_window` at `:3259`); the only missing piece is a producer for that slot, and `reckon/crew/context_budget.py::refusal_census` is the census the consumer's own docstring names as the source, so a fresh guard beside it would duplicate a live consumer whose only gap is an unwired producer
